annotation.title_clean: Establishing a pro-innovation approach to regulating AI
annotation.title_en: Establishing a pro-innovation approach to regulating AI
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS); Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy (BEIS); Office for AI
annotation.summary_en: UK government policy paper (CP 728) proposing a light-touch, context-specific, pro-innovation AI regulatory framework. Existing regulators would apply six non-statutory cross-sectoral principles based on the OECD principles. It rejects the EU's fixed AI definition and invites views through a consultation ahead of a White Paper. Self-driving cars appear only as a case study.
key_provisions_or_claims: Regulate AI by use and context, delegating to existing regulators rather than creating a new central regulator.
Six cross-sectoral principles: safety, technical security, transparency/explainability, fairness, legal-person accountability, and contestability/redress.
Principles initially non-statutory; regulators encouraged to use guidance and voluntary measures first.
No universal AI definition; set out core characteristics of adaptiveness and autonomy instead.
Consultation open until 26 September 2022, ahead of a White Paper in late 2022.
